text:
maya: heads-up — noticed recurring tail-latency spikes in us-west shared-gpu pools around 03:10–03:30 UTC for tenants with lots of long-context streaming calls. CPU on the host is fine, but GPU memory pressure + kv-cache churn looks correlated.

ian: can you paste the p95/p99 traces? is this across multiple instances or one hotspot?

maya: p95 only up a bit, p99 jumps from 420ms to ~2.1s for affected tenants. pattern: sustained long sequences (>8k tokens) from a few tenants + many small requests colliding. Logs show repeated cache invalidations: 

ops-bot: autoscaler/cluster: scale-down prevented for pool-usw-3 (noisy_neighbor_mitigation=active)

maya: sample log snippet: 

```
2026-01-27T03:12:08Z host-12 container[runtime]: KV_CACHE_EVICT tenant=acme-corp keys=134 evict_cycle=3
2026-01-27T03:12:08Z host-12 container[runtime]: OOM_MIGRATION triggered model=redwood-2-xx quant=fp16 pstate=3
2026-01-27T03:12:09Z host-12 container[network]: connection_setup latency=1.2s tenant=acme-corp
```

maya: my read: noisy neighbor is long-context streaming that pins KV cache and causes active eviction thrashing for other tenants sharing the same GPU.

sasha: +1. Are these tenants on the newly launched slice-sharing pools or legacy v1 shared pools?

maya: mostly the slice-sharing ones with dynamic packing.

diego: two quick options: 1) short-term routing change: mark long-context/streaming requests with isolation_score and route them to dedicated-warm pools; 2) mid-term: implement proactive shielding — keep small reserved per-az warm slots for heavy-tenants to avoid cross-tenant eviction.

ian: how would routing mark look? we want something cheap to evaluate.

diego: proposal (quick config): 

```
routing_rules:
  - match: request.features.long_context == true || request.features.stream == true
    action: prefer_pools
    params:
      preferred: [dedicated-warm, dedicated-burst]
      fallback: [shared,pool-default]
      isolation_score_boost: 25
```

sasha: that seems straightforward. cost impact? dedicated-warm means reserved GPUs even when idle. need numbers.

diego: estimate: reserving 2xA10 per AZ as warm for high-tenants ~ $3k/month/az. If it prevents OOM migrations and reduces p99 we save customer SLO hits and fewer expensive fallback spins. Also reduces cache churn which lowers per-token GPU cycles.

maya: alternative cheaper: aggressive prefix caching -> pin first N tokens of long streams to host-local persistent cache, reduce eviction churn. cheaper but complex to implement across runtime.

ian: can we do a hybrid — small 1-GPU warm slot + prefix pin?

diego: yes. start with a 1-GPU warm slot per-az and short prefix pin (first 512 tokens) feature flagged. roll for 48h and measure p99.

maya: I'll open a canary rollout PR for routing change + feature flag for prefix pin. Plan: enable on usw-3 only, observe 72h.

sasha: also please add a billing tag so finance can track dedicated-warm usage.

maya: noted. PR will include tag: redwood:shielding:canary-usw-3.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for config/routing v2.17 -> pool-usw-3 (who=maya, window=72h) :rocket:

ian: thanks — after 24h if we see no regressions let's scale to usw-1 and usw-2. If p99 still bad we revert and consider bigger reserved capacity.

diego: one more thing — add alert: (noisy_neighbor_evictions > 5/min) for a pool triggers temporary tenant-throttling policy (soft-shed) before full migration so we avoid mass migrations.

maya: will add to PR and the runbook. copying runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/noisy-neighbor-shielding

sasha: great. tl;dr: short-term routing + 1-GPU warm-per-az + prefix pin FF. measure p99 & cost over 72h.

maya: thanks team. I'll post updates in this thread once the canary has 24h and 72h reports. :thumbsup:
